concepts.preferred_label: Acute myocardial infarction due to right coronary artery occlusion
aliases: Acute MI due to RCA occlusion
concepts.why: The patient presented with chest pain, elevated serum troponin I level, and ST-segment elevations, which are indicative of acute myocardial infarction, and the total occlusion in the proximal right coronary artery suggests that the infarction is due to right coronary artery occlusion.

The patient's right atrium and right ventricle are located on the left side, and the left atrium and left ventricle are located on the right side, which is consistent with dextrocardia with situs inversus, and the negative P waves in lead I also support this diagnosis.
The patient presented with chest pain, elevated serum troponin I level, and ST-segment elevations, which are indicative of acute coronary syndrome.

rationales.F10: The abnormal position of the heart chambers is consistent with dextrocardia with situs inversus.
rationales.F11: ST-segment elevations are a common ECG finding in acute myocardial infarction.
